title: Alcaraz Keeps Winning — Even With a Sore Leg
summary:
Carlos Alcaraz is on fire — and now he is through to the knockout stage of the ATP Finals. The 23-year-old Spaniard beat world number five Daniil Medvedev 6-2, 6-4 in just 72 minutes in Turin, controlling the match from start to finish.

It was Alcaraz's 11th win in a row. The seven-time major winner has been in sensational late-season form, following back-to-back titles at the Vienna Open and the Paris Masters.

There was one worry. Alcaraz finished the match with heavy strapping on his upper-left leg, and later said he had felt 'a little problem' with his hamstring. 'Right now I'm just feeling OK,' he said.

Asked what pleased him most about his performance, Alcaraz replied: 'Everything'. 'I returned really well, really aggressively, and really deep,' he added. 'I think I just hit the ball in a sweet spot every time. I'm really happy about it.'

His place in the semi-finals was confirmed by Tiafoe's win against Flavio Cobolli, and Alcaraz is scheduled to face Cobolli in his final group match on Friday.
why_it_matters: Alcaraz is one of the best young tennis players in the world, and watching him win — even with a sore leg — shows how hard top players work.
